blocks.text: More Coquitlam real estate
Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: streets and boundaries

items.t: Park Ridge Estates is the established subdivision at the southern base of Burke Mountain in northeast Coquitlam, centred on the David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road corner; no City-published boundary for the subdivision name was found.

The City frames Burke Mountain growth through three neighbourhood plans — Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek — and Park Ridge Estates sits in the built, lower part of that planning area, below the newer Smiling Creek streets.

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: the housing stock

items.t: The stock here is built-out detached houses and townhouse clusters from Burke Mountain's first building phase, not presale product: the new-build supply on Burke Mountain is concentrated in the Smiling Creek and Partington Creek plans above and east of this subdivision.
The named elementary school on the subdivision's own streets is Leigh Elementary, 1230 Soball Street, School District No. 43 (Coquitlam).

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Creek-adjacent lots need an early check: the City flags any lot with a creek on or next to it for a Development Services conversation before design work starts.

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Burke Mountain Discovery Centre, 3537 Princeton Avenue, is the City's sales and information point for the mountain, north of this subdivision in Smiling Creek.
The future village library branch will be inside the Burke Mountain Community Centre; there is no library branch in the subdivision today.
A dedicated Streamside Protection and Enhancement Area protects the natural watercourses on the community centre site, a reminder that creek corridors cross the mountain's development land.

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: development and new projects

items.t: Burke Mountain Village, Burke Mountain, City of Coquitlam village centre, mixed residential and about 120,000 square feet of retail and commercial space including a grocery store, a public plaza and a greenway within 39 acres — status: village lands in development (as of November 3, 2026).

Burke Mountain Community Centre and Burke Village Park, Burke Village, City of Coquitlam, recreation centre with pool, fitness, gymnasium, library branch and multi-purpose rooms plus an adjoining park: design reached 100% complete, the project broke ground in May 2026 and full building construction was expected to begin later in 2026 — status: under construction (as of November 3, 2026).
43, combined middle and secondary school: approximately 70% complete in August 2026 — status: under construction (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: getting around

items.t: There is no SkyTrain station on Burke Mountain; rail access is from the Millennium Line stations below the mountain, reached by bus or car down David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road.
David Avenue is the subdivision's east–west spine across the mountain's base, and Coast Meridian Road is its north–south link down to Lougheed Highway and Port Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Park Ridge Estates Coquitlam: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the City's environmental development permit mapping for any lot here: it maps unstable slopes and watercourse areas, and Burke Mountain lots can carry slope or creek conditions the mapping shows but does not resolve for a specific lot.

Check the creek layer before valuing an addition: Hyde Creek and its tributaries drain the lower mountain through this part of Coquitlam, and the City monitors its creeks for flow, level and water quality.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Park Ridge Estates?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 2 houses listed in Park Ridge Estates. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Park Ridge Estates from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 0 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Park Ridge Estates over those 5 months.

faq.q: How big is Park Ridge Estates compared with the rest of Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, Park Ridge Estates held 0.5% of the 378 detached houses listed in Coquitlam.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Park Ridge Estates than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was 1 in June and 2 in October 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: Which schools serve Park Ridge Estates?
faq.a: Leigh Elementary, 1230 Soball Street, is the elementary school on the subdivision's streets, and the Burke Mountain Middle/Secondary School off David Avenue east of Coast Meridian Road is under construction. School District No. 43 catchment is by permanent home address, so run the exact address in the district locator rather than assuming the closest school is the assigned one.

faq.q: Is Park Ridge Estates the same as Burke Mountain?
faq.a: No — it is one built subdivision at Burke Mountain's southern base, while Burke Mountain is the whole mountainside planning area the City guides through the Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek neighbourhood plans. Services marketed to the wider mountain, including Burke Mountain Village, are north and east of this subdivision, not inside it.

faq.q: What is being built near the subdivision?
faq.a: The Burke Mountain Community Centre and Burke Village Park broke ground in May 2026, with design complete and full building construction following in 2026, beside a village centre planned at about 120,000 square feet of retail including a grocery store. Those amenities serve the whole mountain; nothing under construction inside the subdivision itself was confirmed.

faq.q: Can I add units to a house lot here?
faq.a: The local checks come first: a creek on or beside the lot, a steep slope, or a house built before 1945 each trigger a Development Services conversation before design, and slopes and creek corridors are common on Burke Mountain's lower streets.
